title: LuxEmbedder: A Cross-Lingual Approach to Enhanced Luxembourgish Sentence Embeddings
read_from: arXiv copy (2412.03331v2) of the COLING 2025 paper
subcategory: low-resource language adaptation of a cross-lingual sentence encoder
task: Sentence embeddings for Luxembourgish (cross-lingual transfer, bitext mining, zero-shot classification, paraphrase detection)
problem: Sentence embedding models depend on parallel data that is scarce for low-resource languages such as Luxembourgish, and benchmarks for these languages are missing.
architecture: LaBSE fine-tuned on newly mined human-written parallel sentences (LuxAlign: news articles aligned with text-embedding-3-small, sentences extracted with LaBSE); new ParaLux paraphrase-detection benchmark with GPT-4o-generated, human-corrected adversarial negatives; cross-lingual alignment analysed with CKA on Flores-200.
llm_or_encoder: LaBSE (encoder); GPT-4o only for benchmark construction

datasets.name: Flores-200
datasets.details: used to measure cross-lingual alignment with CKA

key_results: LuxEmbedder accuracy: CL transfer 83.39, bitext mining 70.24, zero-shot classification 65.59, ParaLux 52.24 vs LaBSE 80.88 / 70.11 / 43.24 / 38.14.
Only OpenAI text-embedding-3-large is better on cross-lingual transfer (86.25).
strengths: Shows that a small, high-quality parallel set improves a low-resource language.
Including a low-resource language in parallel training improves alignment of other low-resource languages more than high-resource pairs.

limitations.text: No comparison against general-purpose generative LLMs, which may outperform it on some tasks.
Parallel data is limited to the news domain.
